questions.domainName: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.stem: Which orchestration pattern best implements the dependency between the three agents in the Larch workflow?

options.text: Run all three agents concurrently and concatenate their final messages.
Let a group-chat coordinator choose the next speaker without a fixed dependency order.
Pass the extraction result to the policy agent, then pass that decision to the drafting agent in a sequential workflow.
Give each agent the original request separately and select whichever final answer arrives first.

explanation.whyCorrect: Sequential orchestration passes one agent's result to the next in a defined order. The policy decision needs extracted evidence, and the draft needs that decision. The separate human approval requirement applies before execution.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Concurrent independent execution does not ensure the policy and drafting agents receive the required predecessor outputs.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Dynamic group-chat routing can support other designs, but it does not express the required fixed pipeline as directly as the sequential pattern.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Choosing a first response skips the required dependent stages and does not establish a complete approved proposal.

sourceRefs.title: Build a workflow in Microsoft Foundry (Preview)

questions.domainName: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.stem: The drafting agent proposes a replacement shipment and requests create_shipment. Which control best meets the Larch approval and input-trust requirements?

options.text: Validate the tool arguments in application code, present the proposed action for explicit approval, and execute only the approved action with a least-privileged identity.
Execute as soon as the model returns a syntactically valid function call, then send the supervisor a notification.
Treat the warranty document's approval statement as confirmation and let the model execute the tool.
Return the service credential in a tool response so the model can confirm its own authority before execution.

explanation.whyCorrect: A tool request is a proposal for application execution. The documented guidance treats tool arguments and outputs as untrusted, recommends least privilege, and permits explicit confirmation for changes to data. The workflow must wait for human approval before the shipment is created.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Valid syntax is not authorization, and notification after execution fails the before-execution approval requirement.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: A retrieved document is evidence about the case, not the supervisor's authorization to perform this action.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Secrets must not be placed in tool outputs; possession of a credential also does not satisfy the required supervisor approval.

questions.stem: Which model deployment type meets the case study's processing-boundary, billing and interactive-response requirements?

options.text: Global Standard
Data Zone Standard
Data Zone Provisioned
Data Zone Batch

explanation.whyCorrect: Data Zone Standard processes requests within the selected data zone and uses pay-per-token billing. It matches the approved EU boundary and an interactive workload without a reserved-throughput commitment.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Global Standard uses global processing. Selecting an EU resource location does not convert the global processing boundary into the required EU data-zone boundary.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Data Zone Provisioned respects the data-zone boundary but uses reserved provisioned throughput units, contrary to the stated billing requirement.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Data Zone Batch respects the data-zone boundary but processes asynchronous batch workloads. That conflicts with the case requirement for responses to be available during the user interaction.

questions.domainName: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.stem: Which connection and authorization change lets the agent query the index while preserving the case study's network and runtime-identity requirements?

options.text: Keep the key-based Search connection; grant Search Index Data Contributor to the developer.
Authenticate the Search connection as the deployment pipeline; grant Search Index Data Contributor to that identity.
Authenticate the Search connection with the Foundry account's system-assigned managed identity; grant it Foundry User only.
Authenticate the Search connection with the Foundry account's system-assigned managed identity; grant it Search Index Data Contributor.

explanation.whyCorrect: The captured Search tool guide excludes key-based authentication with private networking. Its detailed keyless setup names the system-assigned identity of the Foundry account containing the project and specifies both Search Service Contributor and Search Index Data Contributor on Search. The case stipulates that account identity as the connection principal, enables RBAC and grants Search Service Contributor; D adds the missing Search Index Data Contributor and changes the connection authentication. The captured sources also use the term 'project managed identity' (S040 line 5 and S011 line 74), while S040 lines 45 and 887 name the account identity. The case stipulation settles the principal for this item; it does not resolve that broader documentation wording conflict. Provisioning permissions on a developer or pipeline do not replace the connection principal's resource access.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: The captured tool guide does not support key-based authentication with private virtual networking. Keeping the key leaves that unsupported authentication method in place; granting a Search role to the developer does not change the agent connection's authentication.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: The documented keyless setup uses the containing Foundry account's system-assigned identity. The pipeline is a provisioning identity in this case, not the configured runtime principal.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: This option does not grant Search Index Data Contributor on the Search service, which the captured keyless setup requires in addition to Search Service Contributor.

questions.domainName: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.stem: Complete the three settings for a supported model using strict structured outputs through the Responses API. Every successful, non-refusal structured output must contain order_id and note; when no note exists, note must be null. Extra properties must be disallowed. The property definitions below are already correct.

artifact.title: Existing property definitions (illustrative JSON Schema fragment)

options.text: Required-property list
Extra-property setting
Request format location

explanation.whyCorrect: The strict schema includes both properties in required. The existing string-or-null type represents an absent note without omitting its key. additionalProperties must be false. For the Responses API, the strict JSON-schema format is configured under text.format; response_format is the Chat Completions location.

whyDistractorsWrong.required: Choose ["order_id", "note"]. Choosing only ["order_id"] omits note from the required list, and [] makes neither field required. The captured strict-schema subset requires all defined fields; nullable values provide optional semantics.
whyDistractorsWrong.additional: Choose false. true permits fields outside the declared contract and violates the documented strict-schema requirement. Nullability of note does not permit extra object properties.
whyDistractorsWrong.format: Choose text.format for Responses. response_format belongs to Chat Completions. JSON mode alone guarantees valid JSON without enforcing this schema.

sourceRefs.title: Structured outputs

questions.domainName: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.stem: Two function requests in a Responses flow call the same local function for different products. Both local executions succeed. Which change is required when returning the outputs shown in this illustrative trace?

artifact.title: Illustrative application trace, not a captured Azure error

options.text: Keep get_stock as call_id and send the two outputs in the same order as the requests.
Combine both results into one output and use get_stock as the identifier for the combined call.
Return each result with its originating call_id: call_red for R-14 and call_blue for B-27.
Replace call_id with the function name in a tool_call_id field while retaining function_call_output.

explanation.whyCorrect: The documented flow returns each function_call_output with the call_id of the function_call it answers. In this trace, get_stock is the function name shared by both invocations; call_red and call_blue identify the separate calls. Returning each result with its originating ID follows that documented pattern and preserves the association before the model continues.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: The documented pattern copies the originating call_id into each result. Keeping the shared name get_stock in that field does not follow the pattern, even when results are sent in request order.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: The model requested two distinct calls. Merging their results under the shared function name fails to return outputs associated with the two originating call IDs.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The captured function_call_output example uses call_id populated from the originating call. This option removes that field and substitutes a function name under another field, so it does not follow the shown pattern.

questions.domainName: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.stem: A user asks an agent for quotes from two carriers and a comparison table with delivery dates. Traces show successful calls to both carriers with correct parameters. The agent follows its system policy against modifying records, but its final response includes only one quote and no comparison table. Which evaluator most directly measures this failure to deliver the requested outcome?

options.text: Task Completion (preview)
Tool Call Success
Task Adherence (preview)
Groundedness

explanation.whyCorrect: Task Completion evaluates whether the agent produced a usable deliverable meeting all user requirements. Successful carrier calls and compliance with the system policy do not establish that the requested two-carrier comparison was delivered.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Tool Call Success measures technical success or errors in tool execution. Both calls succeeded here, so that measure does not directly capture the omitted final deliverable.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Task Adherence measures compliance with assigned rules, procedures and policy constraints. The stated system policy was followed; the described failure is incomplete task delivery.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Groundedness checks fidelity to supplied context. The single quote could be fully grounded while the response still omits the second quote and comparison table.

questions.domainName: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.stem: A support agent needs three kinds of context: a user's preferred delivery time learned across conversations, the company's curated warranty manual, and a receipt uploaded for the current interaction. Which assignment follows the captured Foundry memory guidance?

options.text: Store all three in conversation state and discard the session after every request.
Put the warranty manual in interaction-derived memory and use the organizational knowledge base only for the temporary receipt.
Use file search as the only store for all prior conversational preferences and corporate policies.
Use persistent memory for learned preferences, a curated knowledge base for the manual, and file search for the uploaded receipt.

explanation.whyCorrect: The guidance separates persistent interaction-derived memory, curated organizational knowledge, and search over user-provided documents. These have different retention and grounding purposes.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Current-session state alone does not provide the required context across later sessions.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: This reverses the documented roles of organizational grounding and interaction-derived memory.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: File search is suited to user-provided documents; treating it as the sole mechanism erases the documented distinction between learned memory and governed organizational content.

Construct AIProjectClient with the new project endpoint and an Entra credential, then obtain its OpenAI client with get_openai_client().
Construct AIProjectClient with the new project endpoint but use a resource API key as its only credential.
Use a raw OpenAI client at the Azure OpenAI v1 endpoint and assume it also exposes Foundry project connection-management operations.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: The endpoint is appropriate, but the captured AI Projects client requires Entra authentication rather than key-only authentication.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The raw Azure OpenAI v1 API and Foundry project API are distinct surfaces. Project connection management belongs to the project client, not that raw inference endpoint.

questions.domainName: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.stem: A RAG answer directly addresses the user's question but adds a warranty extension that appears nowhere in the supplied passages. You want an evaluator focused on whether the answer is supported by its context. Which metric best fits?

options.text: Response Completeness, using a reference answer, as the sole test of contextual support.
Document Retrieval, using relevance labels for retrieved documents, as the sole test of generated claims.
Groundedness, comparing the generated response with its supplied context.
Relevance, judging whether the answer addresses the query, without checking its context.

explanation.whyCorrect: Groundedness evaluates alignment of generated content with the supplied context and is directed at unsupported fabrication. A response can be relevant to the question while adding unsupported claims.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Completeness asks whether expected information is covered; coverage alone does not establish that every additional claim is supported.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Retrieval quality evaluates the retrieved material, not whether the generator introduced a new unsupported claim.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: An on-topic response can still fabricate details. Query relevance does not replace contextual support checking.

questions.domainName: Implement generative AI and agentic solutions
questions.stem: An agent performs retrieval, a model call and a tool invocation. End-to-end latency increased, and engineers need to identify the slow operation and its parent request. Which instrumentation provides the most useful structure?

options.text: Keep only a daily total of completed requests.
Record one final answer string for each request without operation timings.
Store one unrelated log line per service without a shared request correlation.
Create a trace for each request and nested spans for the operations, including timings and consistent attributes, exported to Application Insights.

explanation.whyCorrect: A trace represents the request journey. Spans describe timed operations and may be nested, allowing the team to connect latency within a step to its enclosing request.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Daily totals cannot locate an individual slow retrieval, model call or tool operation.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: The final text lacks the operation timing and parent-child relationships needed for this diagnosis.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Uncorrelated logs make reconstructing the request path harder and do not provide the requested trace/span structure.

sourceRefs.title: Agent tracing overview

questions.domainName: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.stem: A team assigns narrow Foundry RBAC roles to developers but its application still authenticates with a shared resource API key. They expect those user-role restrictions to limit each call. Which change addresses that expectation?

options.text: Use Microsoft Entra authentication with the intended scoped role assignments.
Keep the shared API key and add narrower roles to the same users.
Restrict the application to a private network while continuing to authenticate with the shared API key.
Use a different copy of the same API key for each developer.

explanation.whyCorrect: The captured access-control guide states that RBAC restrictions apply with Entra authentication, while key-based access grants access without those role restrictions. The authentication method must support the intended authorization design.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Adding roles does not make a shared key carry per-user role restrictions.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Network isolation restricts connectivity; it does not make key-authenticated requests subject to per-user Entra role assignments.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Copies of the same key do not establish distinct Entra identities or role-scoped calls.

questions.stem: After an ingestion run, most documents appear in an Azure AI Search index, but several known source documents are missing. What should you inspect first to diagnose document-specific failures?

Only the language model's tokens-per-minute allocation.
The indexer execution status, including run timing and detailed item-level errors and warnings.
The answer-generation temperature used by the application.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: A model quota by itself does not show the indexer's item-level processing errors.

questions.domainName: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.stem: An agent team wants to correlate poor answers with evaluation runs. Tool arguments may contain account identifiers and an access token. Which telemetry policy best preserves diagnostic value while following the captured tracing guidance?

options.text: Record every raw argument and credential so any operation can be reproduced exactly.
Remove all trace identifiers, timestamps and evaluation IDs before exporting any data.
Export raw spans first and rely entirely on a nightly script to remove secrets later.
Keep consistent operation and evaluation identifiers, redact sensitive fields before export, and apply log-equivalent access and retention controls.

explanation.whyCorrect: The tracing guide recommends consistent attributes and evaluation-run correlation while removing or masking personal data, secrets and credentials before telemetry storage. Trace data needs appropriate access and retention controls.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: The guidance explicitly excludes secrets and credentials from prompts, tool arguments and span attributes retained in telemetry.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Removing useful nonsecret correlation fields prevents the intended quality/performance analysis and is not required by the redaction guidance.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Redacting only after export leaves sensitive material in telemetry before the cleanup runs, contrary to the stated before-storage guidance.

questions.domainName: Implement computer vision solutions
questions.stem: An app uses the captured Azure Content Safety image:analyze API contract (2024-09-01). Its policy checks all four harm categories, rejects an image when any category is Medium or High, and otherwise allows it. Which TWO implementation choices match that policy and the documented image API?

options.text: Allow any image when the API returns HTTP success, because successful analysis means the content is approved.
Reject when any returned category has severity 4 or 6; otherwise allow the image under the stated policy.
Request EightSeverityLevels for images and reject only severity values 5, 6 or 7.
Request only the Violence category, because it includes the other three harm categories.
Analyze all four categories using FourSeverityLevels, whose documented values are 0, 2, 4 and 6.

explanation.whyCorrect: The documented image moderation contract supports FourSeverityLevels: 0 Safe, 2 Low, 4 Medium and 6 High. Analyzing all four categories and rejecting any result at 4 or 6 implements the stated rule. HTTP success indicates successful analysis; the app still applies its acceptance policy.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Successful analysis is not itself a content-approval decision. The result supplies category severities, and acceptance depends on the configured policy.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: The captured image API supports FourSeverityLevels, not the proposed eight-level output. The proposed threshold also fails to follow the stated Medium-or-High rule for the documented values.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Hate, SelfHarm, Sexual and Violence are separate categories. Requesting only Violence omits signals that the policy explicitly requires.

sourceRefs.title: QuickStart: Analyze image content

questions.domainName: Implement computer vision solutions
questions.stem: A Sora 2 preview v1 remix call returns a new video ID with status queued. Which TWO actions correctly continue the asynchronous workflow to obtain the edited media?

options.text: Track the job for the newly returned video ID until it completes successfully.
Download the original video ID immediately because remix overwrites its media in place.
Treat the queued JSON response itself as the completed video file.
After successful completion, retrieve the content associated with the new video ID.
Submit the same remix repeatedly until a call returns a binary video instead of a job.

explanation.whyCorrect: The remix starts a new asynchronous video job. Track that returned job and retrieve its resulting media after completion. A queued acknowledgment is not the finished media.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: The returned new ID identifies the requested remix; using the original ID retrieves the original media rather than the new result.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: The response contains job metadata, not the finished media payload.
whyDistractorsWrong.E: Repeated submissions create additional work rather than following the documented status-and-retrieval lifecycle.

questions.stem: An AI assistant proposes alt text for a webpage. A magnifying-glass image is the only label on a search button, and a decorative wave adds no information. Which TWO recommendations follow the captured W3C decision tree?

options.text: Describe the search icon's exact color and pixel dimensions instead of naming its action.
Give the search button an accessible text alternative that communicates its search action.
Use the decorative wave's filename as its alt text.
Omit the alt attribute on the decorative image and rely on the browser to choose a description.
Use an empty alt attribute for the purely decorative wave.

explanation.whyCorrect: Functional images need text that communicates the action or destination. Purely decorative images use an empty alt attribute so they do not add unnecessary spoken content.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Appearance alone does not communicate what activating the button does.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: A filename adds irrelevant information for an image with no informative purpose.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The decision tree calls for an empty alt attribute, which is an explicit choice rather than an absent attribute.

questions.stem: A speech-to-text application consistently misrecognizes specialized equipment terms. The team has representative domain recordings and transcriptions. Which TWO activities match the documented Custom Speech workflow?

Select a different text-to-speech voice as the sole repair to the speech recognizer.
Deploy the selected custom recognition model to a custom endpoint for the application.

Assume customization guarantees perfect recognition and remove accuracy evaluation.

questions.domainName: Implement text analysis solutions
questions.stem: A Python Speech SDK application must recognize Italian speech, translate it into German, and later speak the translated text. Recognition and synthesis credentials are already available. Which TWO statements correctly describe this flow?

options.text: Set the recognition source language to de-DE because German is the output language.
Set speech_recognition_language to it-IT and add de as a translation target.
Read result.translations["it-IT"] as the German target output.
Read the German translated text from the de entry after successful translation, then send that text to the synthesis step.
Treat configuring a translation target as proof that a separate SpeechSynthesizer has already produced audio.

explanation.whyCorrect: The source locale identifies the incoming speech, while a target language selects the translation. The translations dictionary is keyed by target language. Generating spoken output is a further synthesis operation.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: German is the target, not the language being recognized from the incoming Italian audio.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: The requested target is de; it-IT is the recognition locale and is not the configured German translation key.
whyDistractorsWrong.E: A configured target or a text translation does not establish that the separate synthesis step has produced audio.

questions.domainName: Implement information extraction solutions
questions.stem: An existing Search pipeline has an index and an embedding deployment configured. The source documents are too long for one embedding request. Arrange the four data-processing steps in dependency order. Configuration setup is complete; these are the operations on each document.

options.text: Split the retrieved text into chunks within the embedding model's input limits.
Write the resulting chunk text and vectors into the configured search index.
Retrieve the raw document content from the supported data source.
Generate an embedding vector for each prepared text chunk.

explanation.whyCorrect: The indexer retrieves source content, chunking prepares units small enough for embedding, the embedding skill produces vectors, and the index receives the processed content. Keeping text as well as vectors supports readable retrieval results.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Chunking follows content retrieval and precedes embedding for these oversized documents.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: The index receives the generated text/vector records after those records exist.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: The raw input must be retrieved before the downstream operations can process it.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The model embeds the prepared chunks; writing finished vector records depends on that output.

questions.stem: Match each hosted-agent failure situation to the most appropriate listed next action. Required session state must be retained, moving regions is prohibited, and the model token quota is not exhausted. Use each selected action once; one action is unused.

options.text: session_quota_exceeded; several sessions no longer need active compute, but their stored state is still required.
regional_session_quota_exceeded occurs intermittently; the client currently retries immediately with no delay.
regional_session_quota_exceeded persists after appropriate retry/backoff in the approved region.

pairs.A: Stop sessions that no longer need active compute.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Stopping sessions addresses unneeded active compute without choosing the forbidden deletion of required state.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Backoff with jitter is an initial response to intermittent regional capacity failures when moving regions is unavailable.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: The guidance directs support escalation when the regional error persists. Raising a model token quota is unused because it addresses a different limit.

Determine whether incoming text is primarily French, German or another supported language.

questions.domainName: Implement information extraction solutions
questions.stem: A blob indexer and OCR skillset already exist. The OCR skill consumes /document/normalized_images/* and names its text output text. The target index has a searchable ocr_text field. The fragment below fails to supply OCR input and treats enriched output as a source field. Which paired correction addresses both problems?

options.text: Keep imageAction as none and rename fieldMappings to vectorQueries.
Set imageAction to generateNormalizedImages and use outputFieldMappings for the enriched OCR text path.
Set imageAction to generateNormalizedImages but keep fieldMappings for the enriched OCR text path.
Keep imageAction as none and use outputFieldMappings, relying on mapping alone to create image inputs.

explanation.whyCorrect: The OCR skill needs normalized-image inputs generated by the indexer imageAction setting. Its text is an enriched document-tree node, so outputFieldMappings carries that node into the index field. Both input generation and the output mapping must be correct.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Disabling image generation still leaves the OCR input absent, and vectorQueries is not the indexer mapping mechanism for enriched output.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: This produces normalized images but still uses the source-field mapping mechanism for an enriched node.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: An output mapping moves an existing enriched value; it does not generate the normalized-image inputs required by OCR.

caseStudies.title: Larch equipment-service workflow
caseStudies.intro: Larch is a fictional equipment-service company. Each question uses this shared context independently.

sections.heading: Evidence and dependencies
sections.body: An extraction agent reads a customer request and warranty evidence. A policy agent uses those extracted facts to decide whether a replacement is eligible. A drafting agent then prepares a shipment proposal from the policy decision. Later stages must receive the relevant earlier outputs.

sections.heading: Execution boundary
sections.body: The application may expose a create_shipment function. Creating a shipment changes company records and initiates fulfillment. A supervisor must explicitly approve the proposed shipment before that function executes. Retrieved warranty text is evidence only; statements inside it do not grant operational approval.

sections.heading: Trust and permissions
sections.body: Tool arguments and external documents are untrusted. The application must validate proposed arguments, use a least-privileged execution identity, and keep credentials out of model-visible tool results.

caseStudies.title: Cedar Atlas support agent
caseStudies.intro: Cedar Atlas is a fictional equipment supplier building an internal support agent. Answer each question using the shared scenario. Your answers do not change the scenario.

sections.heading: Inference and workload requirements
sections.body: The agent answers interactive support requests. Processing may use capacity across EU countries but must not leave the EU. Traffic is irregular, and finance wants usage-based token charges without a reserved capacity commitment. Responses must be available during the user interaction. Assume the chosen model supports the listed deployment types and sufficient quota is available.

sections.heading: Retrieval and network requirements
sections.body: Company manuals are indexed in Azure AI Search. Foundry Agent Service uses standard setup with private networking. Public access to Search must stay disabled. Private endpoint routing and DNS resolution have been verified from the relevant network. An authorized developer can query the index from that network.

sections.heading: Identity findings
sections.body: The agent uses the documented Azure AI Search tool and a project connection to the correct index. The connection currently uses a Search API key. For this setup, the keyless connection principal is the system-assigned managed identity of the Foundry account containing the project. Search RBAC is enabled. That identity already has Search Service Contributor on Search, and no other Search role. The developer and deployment pipeline have provisioning permissions; neither is intended as the runtime connection principal. The agent's model calls already succeed, but its retrieval tool cannot query the company index.
